title: Fix four Unicode and edge-case bugs in Rust text-stats library
description: A Rust text-stats library has four bugs: byte-length instead of char-count, no palindrome normalization, case-sensitive vowel counting, and unsafe Unicode truncation.

task_spec.prompt:
The Rust library in src/lib.rs has four functions with bugs that cause 4 of 6 tests to fail:

1. char_count(s: &str) -> usize — uses s.len() (byte count) instead of s.chars().count()
2. is_palindrome(s: &str) -> bool — does not normalize: ignores case and non-alphanumeric chars
3. count_vowels(s: &str) -> usize — only counts lowercase vowels (misses A, E, I, O, U)
4. char_truncate(s: &str, max_len: usize) -> String — slices at byte offset, not char boundary

Fix all four bugs so that cargo test passes all 6 tests. Do not change the test code. Do not add or remove tests.
required_artifacts: char_count counts Unicode characters not bytes
is_palindrome normalizes case and strips non-alphanumeric
char_truncate is safe on Unicode strings
success_criteria: No new tests added or removed
followup_prompts: Run `cargo test` to check the current state. Walk me through what bugs you found and fixed. If any tests are still failing, show me the errors and fix them.
Final verification: run `cargo test` and confirm a completely clean build. Every test must pass — if any are still red, fix them now.
